newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH MEDIA REMOULD NORMAL INTERNATIONALISATION - PM.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH MEDIA REMOULD NORMAL INTERNATIONALISATION - PM.

text.p: An ongoing reshuffle in the Finnish media industry and foreign ownership should be seen as normal part of internationalisation, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Friday.

Foreign ownership which had boosted capital in the media industry could "lead to a reduction in domestic concentration, or at least balance it," he said in a written speech to the graphic workers' union.
"The media sector reorganisation and the increase in foreign capital should be regarded the result of internationalisation of the economy and the media world," he said.
However, this could also have "negative effects on media content to which we cannot close our eyes". He did not elaborate.
After years of calm, the Finnish media sector started announcing major developments last year.

A second nationwide commercial television station led by leading newspaper group Sanoma and owned partly by foreigners is due to start broadcasting on Sunday and Sanoma also plans to rival publishing group Aamulehti's business daily Kauppalehti with a new paper.

Kauppalehti already operates and on-line news site available on the internet and Sanoma has said its new business paper will work together with its real-time news agency to challenge international providers.
Aamulehti group announced this spring that it will merge with the country's first commercial television operator MTV.
Swedish Marieberg owns 29 percent of the shares in Aamulehti and has said it aims to maintain a 20-25 percent stake in the group after it has merged with MTV.
